sections.title: Bow
sections.info: How a held note moves: the bow's own unsteadiness, measured from the cello's recordings. Every note moves differently.

sections.title: Instrument
sections.info: The cello around the string: its open strings ringing along, a mute on its bridge, its size, and (if you want one) a wolf note.

sections.title: Playing
sections.info: How the notes are played: bowed (held, staccato, spiccato, tremolo, harmonics) or plucked, where the dynamic comes from, how the strings are shared, how long they ring. Keyswitches below the cello's range choose the articulation: C1 Arco, D1 Staccato, E1 Spiccato, F1 Pizzicato, G1 Tremolo, A1 Harmonics.

sections.title: Vibrato
sections.info: The left hand rocking on the string. As the pitch swings, each harmonic sweeps through the body's narrow resonances and its level rises and falls: that, more than the pitch itself, is what a cello's vibrato sounds like.

sections.title: Space
sections.info: The room around the cello. The recordings are dry and close-miked, which is part of why the tone sounds edgy; a hall around it is what a listener hears. Reverb 0 is the dry cello. The same reverb as Piano's: early reflections from a model of each space, a smooth feedback tail, so Decay, Size and Damping can be set freely.

sections.title: LFO
sections.info: A modulation source for anything in the matrix. For vibrato, use the Vibrato panel: it follows the string and wanders as a player's does.
Legato slurs a new key from the held one without a new bow stroke, gliding over Glide (40 ms is a finger change; longer is an expressive portamento). Mono bows each note again.

paramInfo.life.amount: How much the held note moves, all of it together: 100 % is the cello's own, as measured from its recordings (its pitch wandering by about 1.5 cents, its level by about 1.4 dB, each harmonic by 1-3 dB on its own). 0 holds the note perfectly still, which sounds synthetic; up to 300 % is a restless, unsteady bow. Listen to a long held note after its first half second.
paramInfo.life.pitch: The pitch's share of the movement: lower steadies the pitch while the tone keeps moving, higher makes it waver (400 % is about 6 cents, an unsteady hand).
paramInfo.life.flicker: Each harmonic moving on its own, which is most of what makes a bowed note sound alive (the higher harmonics most: about 1.3 dB on the fundamental, 3 dB by the 20th). Lower makes the tone glassy and still; higher makes it shimmer. Easiest to hear on low notes.
paramInfo.life.speed: How fast the movement is: 100 % is the cello's own (most of it slower than 2 Hz for the level, up to 16 Hz for the pitch and the harmonics). Lower is a slow drift; higher is a nervous trembling.
paramInfo.tone.body: How much of the cello's body is in the tone: its resonances, measured from every note of the recordings, which colour each harmonic by where its frequency falls. 0 is the bowed string alone (bare and buzzy); 100 % is the cello; up to 200 % exaggerates the body (hollow and vowel-like). The level stays the same.
paramInfo.tone.noise: The bow's noise, the rosin's hiss under the note: 0 dB as measured, where it sits 35-45 dB under the tone, so a few dB either way is subtle. Lower is a smoother, cleaner tone; +12 dB and up is clearly airy and scratchy. Most audible on soft and high notes.
paramInfo.tone.grain: How the bow noise pulses with the string: in the recordings it comes in bursts, once per vibration, as the bow catches and slips (most in the upper bands). 0 is steady hiss beside the note; 100 % is as measured, the noise woven into the tone; higher is gritty and rasping.
paramInfo.play.release: How long the strings ring after you let go: 100 % is measured from the cello's staccatos (the low notes ring longest). Lower damps them; higher lets them ring on, as an open string would.
paramInfo.play.dynamics: How hard the bow plays the held note, from p (0) to f (100 %), as the cello's recordings were played: louder is also brighter. With Dynamics From set to Controller it follows the mod wheel (CC 1) or expression pedal (CC 11) through the note: swell and fade a held note. With Velocity it isn't used.
paramInfo.play.dynMode: Velocity: each note's velocity sets its dynamic for the whole note. Controller: the velocity sets only the attack (how hard the bow catches the string), and Dynamics (the mod wheel or expression pedal) sets the sustain and can move during it, as a player's bow does.
paramInfo.play.strings: Free plays every key as its own note. One Note Each plays as a cello does: four strings, one note each. A key goes to the highest string tuned below it; a new note on a string that's ringing bows it again (cutting the ring), and if every string that can play it is held, the highest one slurs to it. Chords spread across strings, and five-note chords can't all sound. Works in Poly.
paramInfo.vib.depth: How far the pitch swings either side of the note, in cents, for a note a fifth above its open string; higher up a string the same hand movement swings further, as on the cello. Cellists measure about 10-17 cents; 0 is no vibrato (the recordings have none).
paramInfo.vib.rate: How many times a second the pitch swings: cellists measure about 5.3-6.5 Hz. Slower is a wide, romantic vibrato; faster is intense.
paramInfo.vib.delay: How long after the bow starts the vibrato begins. Players often start a note straight and let the vibrato bloom.
paramInfo.vib.attack: How long the vibrato takes to reach its full depth once it starts.
paramInfo.vib.vary: How much the vibrato's rate and depth wander, as a player's do. 0 is perfectly regular, which sounds mechanical; 100 % is loose and expressive.
paramInfo.bow.weight: How heavily the bow sits on the string, at the same loudness: lighter is sweeter and rounder, heavier is brighter with more edge. It plays the spectrum of the cello's own softer or louder bowing (the recordings' dynamics), so the tone tilts gradually from the 5th harmonic up rather than being cut off. 0 is as recorded.
paramInfo.play.slur: How a slurred note changes (Legato, or One Note Each taking a held string): the tone dips briefly as the finger lifts and lands while the bow goes on, and the vibrato starts again from the note's centre. 0 is a seamless change; 100 % is a clearly articulated one (about 12 dB for 80 ms).
paramInfo.play.even: How even the notes are in loudness. The recorded notes were played a few dB louder or softer each (A3 stands out, A4 is soft); a player keeps a line even. 100 % follows a smooth curve along the keyboard; 0 plays each note as recorded. Each note keeps its own tone either way.
paramInfo.space.room: How much of the space you hear. The recordings are close-miked, so 0 is the dry cello; 25 % puts the room about 11 dB under a held note, 100 % about as loud as it.
paramInfo.space.type: The space: Room (a small room, 0.6 s), Chamber (1.3 s), Hall (a concert hall, 2.2 s), Cathedral (5 s) or Plate (a bright, dense studio plate, 2.4 s, no reflections). Changing it lets the old space ring out.
paramInfo.space.decay: The tail's length against the space's own (its RT60). 100 % is the space as designed.
paramInfo.space.size: Scales the tail's delays: smaller is denser and more metallic, larger is grainier and more spacious. The decay time stays. Moving it while a tail rings bends its pitch a little, like a tape.
paramInfo.space.predelay: A gap before the reverb starts, on top of the space's own distances: a bigger stage, and a clearer attack.
paramInfo.space.damping: How much faster the treble dies than the rest. 50 % is the space's own; 0 % keeps the treble as long as the body (bright, glassy); 100 % makes it die quickly (warm, dark).
paramInfo.space.early: The early reflections' level against the tail: up for a sense of walls close by, down for a tail that blooms on its own.
paramInfo.space.lowcut: Takes the bass out of the reverb only, so low notes don't turn muddy.
paramInfo.space.highcut: Takes the top out of the reverb only, for a softer, more distant space.
paramInfo.string.resonance: The open strings ringing along: a string a note isn't played on picks up the harmonics it shares with that note, and rings on after it. Strongest where a note is in unison with an open string's partial (G3 sets the open G ringing). 0 dB is a faint halo (the recordings already hold the cello's own, while a note is held); +12 dB is a clear halo; +24 dB a shimmering wash; −40 dB off.
paramInfo.body.size: The body's size against the cello's: its resonances move with it, the string stays. Smaller (down to 50 %) moves them up, towards a viola's or violin's body: the low notes lose their depth. Larger (up to 200 %) moves them down, towards a bass's. 100 % is the cello recorded.
paramInfo.body.wolf: A wolf note: on many cellos one note (often between E3 and F#3) fights the body's main resonance and can't settle, stuttering and growling. 0 is none (the recorded cello has none); higher makes it stronger and wider. It is only near the Wolf Note.
paramInfo.body.wolfNote: Where the wolf is. 175 Hz is about F3; most cellos' wolves are between E3 (165 Hz) and F#3 (185 Hz).
paramInfo.bow.position: Where the bow crosses the string. 0 is the normal place (about a tenth of the string from the bridge, as recorded). Towards the fingerboard (sul tasto, down to −100 %) the tone gets soft, round and a little airy; towards the bridge (sul ponticello, up to +100 %) it gets bright, then glassy and whistling, with a scratchier noise. The partials with a node where the bow is are weakened, as on the string.
paramInfo.body.mute: A mute on the bridge. Around 50 % is a performance mute (con sordino): veiled and nasal, a little quieter. 100 % is a heavy practice mute: muffled and much quieter. 0 is no mute.
paramInfo.play.articulation: How the next notes are played (each note keeps the articulation chosen when it starts). Arco: held, bowed. Pizzicato: plucked, the finger's snap as recorded, then the string ringing down as measured. Staccato: a short bowed stroke from the cello's own staccatos (the bow leaves by itself, however long the key is held; louder and longer strokes the harder you play). Spiccato: bounced, shorter and lighter, the string ringing after the bow leaves. Tremolo: rapid bow changes, the cello's own recorded strokes (Tremolo Rate). Harmonics: a finger lightly on the string, a pure, flute-like tone: a natural harmonic of an open string where one sounds at the key, else an artificial one; below C3 no harmonic fits and the note is bowed as usual. Keyswitches (they don't sound): C1 Arco, D1 Staccato, E1 Spiccato, F1 Pizzicato, G1 Tremolo, A1 Harmonics. The Bow panel, Bow Noise, Grain, Bow Weight and Bow Position shape every bowed note but the tremolo's (its strokes are recordings); Dynamics shape held notes (Arco, Tremolo, Harmonics), and Slur joins Arco and Tremolo notes.
paramInfo.play.tremRate: Tremolo: about how many times a second the bow changes direction. The strokes are the cello's own recorded staccatos, each bowed the way it goes, in a player's uneven rhythm around this rate (a long stroke, then a short; the pace drifting). Notes started together share one bow, as in a double stop. Lower is a slower, measured tremolo (6 at least), higher a frantic one.
